title: C# Questions & Answers - Exceptions of Type Finally and Built in Exceptions
sourceFile: C# Questions & Answers - Exceptions of Type Finally and Built in Exceptions - Sanfoundry.html
description: This set of C# Questions and Answers focuses on "Exceptions of Type Finally and Built in Exceptions".

questions.question: Which of these clauses will be executed regardless of whether an exception is thrown or caught?
questions.explanation: The 'finally' block is used to execute a set of statements (typically cleanup code) regardless of whether an exception occurred or was handled in the 'try' or 'catch' blocks.

questions.question: A single 'try' block must be followed by which of the following?

options.text: At least one 'catch' block or a 'finally' block

questions.explanation: A 'try' block cannot exist by itself. It must be followed by at least one 'catch' block, one 'finally' block, or both.

questions.question: Which exception is thrown when integer division by zero occurs in C#?
questions.explanation: Integer division by zero throws DivideByZeroException. It inherits from ArithmeticException, so catching ArithmeticException would also work, but DivideByZeroException is the type that is actually thrown.

questions.question: Which exception occurs if an application attempts to access an array element using an index that is outside the bounds of the array?
questions.explanation: IndexOutOfRangeException is thrown when an attempt is made to index an array outside its lower or upper bounds.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code snippet if run with no command-line arguments?
questions.explanation: If no arguments are passed, 'a' is 0. '1 / 0' throws a DivideByZeroException. Since this inherits from ArithmeticException, the catch block executes and prints '1'.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code snippet?
questions.explanation: The code throws a NullReferenceException. However, the catch block is only designed to handle ArithmeticException. Since the exception is not caught, the program crashes with a runtime error.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code snippet?
questions.explanation: Inside the inner try, 'a' becomes 0. No exception occurs in the inner block. The inner 'finally' executes, printing 'A'. The catch block is never triggered because no IndexOutOfRangeException occurred.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code snippet if run with no command-line arguments?
questions.explanation: With no arguments, 'a' is 0. '10 / 0' immediately throws a DivideByZeroException in the outer try block. Control jumps to the outer catch (ArithmeticException), printing 'TypeB'. The inner try is never entered.

questions.question: Which of these classes is the base class for all exceptions in C#?
questions.explanation: In .NET, all exceptions are objects derived from the System.Exception class.
